rationales.wacc: 11.0% (analyst judgment; no market-rate data is in the snapshot). Built as a cost of equity: assumed risk-free rate of about 4.5%, plus an assumed beta of about 1.3 times an assumed 5.0% equity risk premium, giving about 11.0%. Debt has almost no effect on the weighting. Mapped total debt is $33,366M (F-de060525b4), against a market capitalisation of roughly $5.1T at the $209.66 close on 2026-08-26 times 24,285M diluted shares (F-ce6be3a0b0). So WACC is set equal to the cost of equity. The beta assumption reflects concentrated hyperscaler demand, extended payment terms on large multi-quarter agreements (Q-9), supply commitments of $279B (Q-8) and guarantee obligations of up to $105B (Q-10). It was not chosen to reach any value.
rationales.terminal_growth: 3.0% (judgment): about long-run nominal GDP growth. This is a mature-state assumption for year 6 onward, after explicit-period growth has slowed to 5% in year 5. Kept well below the 11.0% WACC.
rationales.revenue_growth: Year 1 is the NTM revenue that code computes from assumptions.json. The four forecast quarters run from $108.0B (Q-1 midpoint) to about $137B, roughly $492B in total, against TTM revenue of $302,969M (sum of F-296b652672, D-e6100d63c6, F-e3b41ab7aa, F-5b8aab8df3). Year 2 is +25% (judgment). The model's exit rate is +7% q/q in FY2028Q2. If sequential growth keeps slowing by about one point per quarter (6%, 5%, 4%, 3%), the next four quarters total about 26% above the NTM sum. Years 3-5 are +12%, +8% and +5% (judgment): growth fades toward terminal growth to reflect the larger base, possible digestion of customer capex, competition from custom accelerators, and no China data-center compute revenue (Q-2). These rates are judgments, not guidance.
rationales.peers: AMD, AVGO and MRVL, all from config/project.yaml coverage. Like NVIDIA, each is a large fabless designer whose growth is driven by AI data-center silicon: AMD makes merchant GPUs/accelerators and data-center CPUs; AVGO makes custom AI accelerators (ASICs) and data-center networking; MRVL makes custom data-center silicon and optical/electrical interconnect. Excluded: INTC (integrated device maker with a foundry business, different margin and capital profile); MU (memory, commodity-cyclical); AMAT, LRCX and KLAC (wafer-fab equipment); SNPS and CDNS (EDA software); MPWR (power management); ALAB and CRDO (small-cap AI connectivity names whose revenue base and multiples are not comparable to a company of NVIDIA's scale). Peers were chosen on business mix before any multiples were looked at. Code excludes any peer lacking data at the cutoff.
rationales.fcf_margin: Based on history, using FCF = CFO (cfo line) minus capex (capex line) divided by revenue, per quarter, from eu.py history. TTM through FY2027Q2: CFO $134,360M (D-e8c1536e16, D-a809e95cf9, F-1681c07273, D-286ba7c3b2) minus capex $7,354M (D-91d723d96f, D-7cba4ccb7e, F-9e6d2fffc2, D-0158212347) = $127,006M, which is 41.9% of TTM revenue of $302,969M. Over the last eight quarters the figure is 42.5% ($199,029M / $468,187M). Quarterly values are volatile, from 22.2% in FY2027Q2 to 59.5% in FY2027Q1, because of working-capital timing, so we use multi-quarter averages. Capex has been about 2-4% of revenue. Year 1 is 40%, below the TTM figure, because receivables (DSO up to 60 days on extended terms, Q-9), inventory build for Vera Rubin (Q-12) and much larger supply commitments (Q-8) point to continued working-capital absorption. Years 2-3 are 42%, back to the eight-quarter average as the working-capital build normalises. Years 4-5 ease to 41% and 40% for competitive and pricing pressure. The terminal margin of 40% is about two points below history, roughly offsetting share-based compensation, which CFO adds back (about 2.4% of TTM revenue: $7,241M from D-b80c63794a, D-ea178ca430, F-2fe9793dc6, D-b8cb802c09). These margins sit well below the model's after-tax operating margin of about 54% (74% gross margin, about 8.5% opex, 17% tax), consistent with the historical gap between NOPAT and CFO minus capex.
rationales.dcf_weight: 0.7 DCF / 0.3 peer EV/Sales (judgment). The DCF uses the guided next quarter (Q-1) and the explicit growth fade, so it is the primary method. The peer value applies the median TTM EV/Sales of AMD, AVGO and MRVL to NVIDIA's TTM revenue. It is a market cross-check but does not adjust for NVIDIA's far higher margins or its different growth profile, so it gets the smaller weight. Some weight is kept because the DCF depends heavily on the assumed WACC and terminal value (the terminal value is about 71% of DCF EV on these inputs).
